candidates.original_title: Cortical and subcortical contributions to Stop signal response inhibition: role of the subthalamic nucleus
candidates.description: Greater subthalamic nucleus (STN) activity during stop trials compared to go trials during a stop signal task
candidates.citation_sentence: We sought to replicate the finding of greater subthalamic activity during stop compared to go trials, as reported in Aron and Poldrack, 2006.

candidates.original_title: Cortical and subcortical contributions to Stop signal response inhibition: role of the subthalamic nucleus
candidates.description: Stop trials produce greater activity in the subthalamic nucleus than go trials.
candidates.citation_sentence: We sought to replicate the finding of greater subthalamic activity during stop compared to go trials, as reported in Aron and Poldrack, 2006.

candidates.original_title: Cortical and subcortical contributions to Stop signal response inhibition: role of the subthalamic nucleus
candidates.description: Individuals with short SSRT show greater subthalamic nucleus activity than individuals with long SSRT.
candidates.citation_sentence: Specifically, greater STN activity in the short, as compared to the long, SSRT group would replicate the findings of Aron and Poldrack, 2006.
candidates.notes: The replication found the opposite pattern, with greater bilateral STN activity in the long-SSRT group, and states that the STN results contrasted with Aron and Poldrack (2006). [luna56: extra entry, not in the external record]
